thread:
ada: TL;DR propose extracting a small route-sidecar that answers routing+kv-read requests. aim: shrink runtime deploy footprint and enable faster rollout of routing changes without touching hot path. open for feedback.

mike: +1 on smaller blast radius. do we have any numbers on added RTT for a hop?

ada: initial bench (local dev) shows ~3ms median, ~6ms p95; emulated load shows p95 up ~8-10ms when cold. warm caches drop that a lot. these are local-AZ numbers.

chris: curious about consistency model. if sidecar returns a stale mapping and runtime caches it, how do we invalidate?

ada: plan: sidecar is authoritative for mapping. runtime keeps a soft TTL cache and subscribes to a small push-stream for invalidations. fallback: runtime will fallback to previous heavy-path resolver if sidecar errors or signals degraded.

sophia: how minimal is the API surface? prefer a single idempotent endpoint. something like: 
```
POST /route/resolve
{ "session": "s-123", "prefix": "abc" }
-> { "target": "gpu-45", "lease_ms": 30000, "flags": ["hotstart"] }
```
Only returns what runtime needs to pick a node and warm KV. keep auth simple (mTLS).

jordan: ownership question: who pages when the sidecar is flapping? do we add SLOs?

marie: ops suggestion: platform owns sidecar binary + infra (deploy, autoscale, alerting). runtime team owns local integration (cache, fallback, retries). we include runbook steps in RFC.

chris: add a cheap health hint header so runtime can detect partial failure without parsing payload, e.g., `X-Route-State: ok|degraded|draining`. runtime can circuit-break on degraded.

ada: agreed. we'll standardize a header. also thinking about a control flag to force-forget mappings during rollbacks.

mike: constraints: no cross-region calls for initial rollout. keep sidecars inside same AZ. later we can add cross-region read replicas for cold starts.

sophia: testing: I can own integration harness that verifies fallback behaviour, cache-invalidation, and rollout abort paths. will add smoke & chaos tests.

ada: perf plan: mike will run a 1M-request spike against a canary to measure tail. capture p50/p95/p99, cache-hit-rate, and request amplification (extra calls).

mike: noted. will also run memcache vs local in-memory cache comparison for warmup times.

jordan: timeline proposal: spike (2w) -> infra + harness (1w) -> canary in one AZ (2w) -> expand (2w) -> 30d observation. total ~7-8 weeks.

ada: risk register (sketch):
- increased network hop -> p99 regression on cold flows
- cache invalidation races -> sticky misroutings
- rollout complexity causing traffic splits issues
mitigations: push invalidation stream, fallback heavy path, observability deck.

chris: please add a small metrics set to the RFC: route-sidecar_request_count, error_rate, p95_latency, cache_hit_ratio, fallback_rate, rollbacks. we want alert thresholds.

ada: will add. also adding an amortization card: estimate 6 engineer-weeks and a 90-day monitoring runway to ensure tech-debt doesn't increase.

marie: also consider a lightweight feature-flag gate that can quickly disable sidecar per-AZ. handy for fast rollback.

ada: good call. rollout flags in the config: `enabled_per_az`, `circuit_breaker_threshold`, `soft_cache_ttl_ms`.

sophia: UX note: make error payloads terse. runtime will log details; sidecar shouldn't slow things with big JSON.

chris: security: require mTLS + JWT-bearing client certs. avoid adding a new keystore if possible.

ada: agreed. we reuse platform certs and token exchange.

infra-bot: CI: route-sidecar/spike branch - unit tests passed, integration tests queued :gear:.

ada: next steps: I'll open a small RFC follow-up with API contract, rollout YAML snippet, amortization estimate, perf test plan, and the minimal metrics dashboard wireframe. tagging @mike @sophia @chris @marie for quick review.

mike: I'll take the perf spike.

sophia: I'll draft the QA harness.
